# ChatGPT Sites for Federal Government

<!-- vimeo: 1215584300 | track: English (auto-generated) -->

[▶ Watch on Vimeo](https://vimeo.com/1215584300)

<details>
<summary>자막: ChatGPT Sites for Federal Government</summary>

Government teams often rely on information spread across documents, links, and systems. ChatGPT Sites can help turn approved information into a clear, interactive employee experience. Start in ChatGPT Work and describe the website you want to create. Here, we are building a resource hub for a fictional federal agency called the Federal Civic Services Agency. The prompt names the audience, the content to include, accessibility expectations, and important boundaries. It also tells ChatGPT not to use personal information, real policies, or external data. ChatGPT creates a working site that you can review and refine. This example has clear navigation, a topic filter, quick links, upcoming deadlines, and a visible reminder that every item is fictional. Nothing has been shared or published. The site can be interactive. An employee can filter the resources by topic and quickly find the most relevant option. If the first version is not quite right, ask ChatGPT for a change in plain language. For example, make deadlines more prominent, simplify the navigation, or improve keyboard accessibility. The same experience can bring several everyday needs together. Here, fictional deadlines appear beside a first-week checklist. An employee can mark an item complete and immediately see their progress. The goal is not to replace an agency's official systems, but to make approved information easier to find and use. Frequently asked questions can explain where to begin, whether the content is official, and what information may be appropriate to use. Before sharing any site, review the content, links, behavior, access settings, and intended audience. Follow your organization's privacy, security, records, and approval requirements. For this demonstration, the site remains in private preview and uses fictional information only. Start with a narrow employee need, give ChatGPT clear constraints, test the result, and have the appropriate people review it before you share.

</details>
